Use it. Understand its limits.

A repeatable path from purchase to recovery.

How to use the solution

1. Open Working solution.
Select the routine grocery example, then evaluate. Expect approval.
2. Try an unusual purchase.
Select electronics, evaluate, then answer “Yes, this was me” to approve it.
3. Reject a purchase you don’t recognize.
Re-evaluate the unusual example, then choose “No, not me.” Expect a block and a recovery offer.
4. Complete recovery.
Choose “Activate demo digital access.” No real card is created. Uncheck wallet availability and repeat to see the assisted-recovery path.
5. Verify the behavior.
Open Skills & testing and run the workflow checks. Change signals to explore other outcomes.

Expected customer impact

The proposed service aims to reduce unnecessary declines, replace avoidable fraud calls with in-app confirmation, and shorten payment disruption for eligible mobile-wallet users.

The prototype demonstrates the process. It does not measure fraud detection accuracy, customer adoption, or savings.

The deck’s business case

All financial figures below are planning estimates to be validated by Finance. The source deck reports 350K–400K monthly fraud calls; the model uses the 375K midpoint.

Value leverAssumption and calculationAnnual estimate
Fraud losses$250M baseline × 20% reduction$50.0M
Service demand375K calls × 12 × 30% avoided × $6/call$8.1M
Spend recovery / retentionUnvalidated assumption; bank spend and attrition baseline absent$15.0M
Total gross benefitSum of the three levers; before $6M annual run cost$73.1M

One-time investment: $41.25M. Using the deck’s 25% / 75% / 100% three-year benefit ramp and $6M annual run cost yields $146.2M benefits, $59.25M total cost, $86.95M net benefit and approximately 147% ROI. The deck quotes approximately 19-month payback after go-live; validating that timing requires a monthly cash-flow schedule.

Limits and assumptions

Transparent rules simulate the production AI decision engine. Synthetic risk signals have no proven predictive value. There is no issuer connection, authorization, wallet provisioning or real fraud block.

Digital recovery depends on eligible devices and supported wallets. Verification must be authenticated in production. Real customer confirmations would inform retraining only after independent model-risk validation.

The $15M retention estimate is not derived from the dated 2017 Fiserv percentages: the necessary bank spend baseline is missing.

The next realistic improvement

Validate loss, call-cost and false-decline baselines with Finance and Fraud. Then test a production model in shadow mode against existing rules using appropriately governed data.

Proceed to a controlled 5–10% pilot only after independent validation, operational readiness and agreed customer-harm thresholds. Measure fraud-loss rate, false declines, verification completion, calls and recovery activation before scaling.
